body:
This proposal advocates for the inclusion of continuous fuzzing practices (I don't mean DAST), particularly coverage-based fuzzing, within Continuous Deployment (CD) pipelines in the ASVS.

Fuzzing, especially automated fuzzing in CD pipelines, has proven instrumental in identifying and resolving security vulnerabilities that may not be detected by other testing methods. For example I found this bug in Python's pickle module ([Issue 41288](https://bugs.python.org/issue41288)), and I used the AFL fuzzer to find this in a few hours and this bug could lead to denial-of-service (DoS). 

This demonstrates the necessity for coverage-based fuzzing to be part of the standard security testing toolkit in modern development pipelines.

I agree with @elarlang and this is something that has been covered elsewhere although I admit I can't find a good reference.

Basically, in ASVS our scope is the application itself, not the processes around secure development or other security scanners.

We recently had a discussion about where the border is and you can see my response in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1526#issuecomment-1801232706

ASVS 4.x did not strictly hold to this line and this is something we are working on
I am going to respectfully close this for now.
